outline.summary: Title slide with author and affiliation

outline.title: Project Overview
outline.summary: Introduction to the problem statement of modeling a vehicle and evaluating losses

outline.title: Design Choice: 800V Architecture
outline.summary: Justification for 800V architecture to reduce phase currents and ohmic losses

outline.summary: Why 2L-VSI is insufficient at 800V and the need for multilevel topologies

outline.title: Topology Selection: FC vs NPC
outline.summary: Comparison of FC and NPC highlighting thermal symmetry and natural balancing

outline.title: FC Switching States and PD-PWM
outline.summary: Explanation of 3L-FC switching states and natural balancing via PD-PWM with schematic
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/UHnXuYSG0Dhr.png; /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/6Mm7Myhb8PPL.jpg; /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/aTmbb5bAcKaD.png - This slide discusses component selection, specifically mentioning SiC modules. outline.title: Component Selection
outline.summary: Justification for Wolfspeed CAB450M12XM3 SiC module and 680uF film capacitor
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/switching_loss_figures/fig4_vehicle_architecture.png - This slide maps vehicle speed to inverter operating points. Image 11 directly illustrates the relationship between vehicle speed, electrical frequency, peak phase current, and switching frequency, which is highly relevant to the slide's content.

outline.title: Vehicle Architecture Mapping
outline.summary: Mapping mechanical vehicle speed to electrical operating points and current profiles
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/switching_loss_figures/fig1_switching_loss_vs_speed.png - This slide discusses switching loss vs. speed. Image 10, titled 'Switching Loss vs. Vehicle Speed — Effect of fsw', directly visualizes the data and concepts presented in the slide.

outline.title: Switching Loss Analysis
outline.summary: Application of Graovac-Purschel analytical method to SiC MOSFETs
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/switching_loss_figures/fig2_loss_breakdown.png - This slide explains how adaptive switching frequency reduces urban losses. Image 12, 'Loss Breakdown: Adaptive Schedule vs. Fixed 20 kHz', clearly illustrates the reduction in losses with the adaptive schedule.

outline.title: Simulated Adaptive Switching Frequency
outline.summary: Methodology of adapting fsw based on fe to maintain mf and reduce losses
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/thermal_comparison_figures/fig3_Tj_bar_comparison.png - This slide focuses on the thermal impact and junction temperature reduction. Image 17, 'Junction Temperature at Key Operating Points', directly compares junction temperatures for fixed and adaptive schedules, supporting the key points of the slide.

outline.title: Thermal Impact of Adaptive Schedule
outline.summary: Reduction in junction temperature and thermal cycling amplitude
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/fc_inverter_results_v3/fig4_fc_voltages.png - This slide validates the design through simulation, specifically mentioning FC voltage balancing. Image 7, 'Flying Capacitor Voltages (Cfc=680uF, Vfc_ref=400V)', directly shows the FC voltage waveforms and balancing, which is crucial for this slide.

outline.title: Simulation Results
outline.summary: Validation of THD, FC voltage balancing, and pre-charge sequence

outline.summary: Summary of key findings, loss reductions, and future work limitations
